messages:
Maya: Heads-up: CI started failing on feature branch only in GHA (node18). Local vitest/jest runs are green. Error in GH logs: "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" when tests import our JS SDK. Anyone seen this combo?

Sam: Yep. Usually a module-resolution/transform mismatch. We flipped package.json to "type": "module" in the SDK package and some runners treat the package as ESM while others see the CJS build. Vitest often works if you inline the dep; Jest needs explicit ESM config.

Juan: Found an extra twist: pnpm hoisting in the monorepo caused two copies of the SDK artifacts during CI (one ESM, one CJS) and the resolver picked the CJS file without a proper transform. Repro locally by running tests from project root vs workspace package.

Alex: Oof. Two quick mitigations:
1) For vitest add the SDK to deps.inline so esbuild transpiles node_modules entrypoint. Example: `deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference-sdk'] }`.
2) For Jest (if using it) ensure Node 18+ with `--experimental-vm-modules` or use `babel-jest`/`ts-jest` to transform ESM deps. Also check `moduleNameMapper` if hoisting confuses paths.

Maya: Can someone paste a minimal vitest config that actually fixed it for CI? I tried several variants.

Sam: Sure — this worked for our CI runner:
```js
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference-sdk'] },
    esbuild: { target: 'es2022' },
    environment: 'node'
  }
})
```
That plus clearing pnpm cache removed the import error.

Juan: Another flake we saw: mocking shapes differ. When running via esbuild transform the SDK exposes named exports; when loaded as raw ESM it exposes default. Tests using `vi.mock('@redwood/inference-sdk')` and `import sdk from '@redwood/inference-sdk'` intermittently failed with "TypeError: sdk.mockPredict is not a function".

Alex: Workaround: in tests `import * as SDK from '@redwood/inference-sdk'` and then `vi.spyOn(SDK, 'default')` or stub specific named exports. That avoids ambiguity between default vs namespace import shapes. Also add a tiny helper in test utils: `const mockClient = (impl) => { jest.spyOn(SDK, 'default').mockImplementation(() => impl) }`.

Maya: We also hit `ReferenceError: self is not defined` in a couple of tests that require edge compatibility. Our runtime tries `if (typeof self !== 'undefined')` and node envs don't define self. What should tests do?

Sam: For edge semantics either set test environment to jsdom/happy-dom or add a setup file that polyfills: `global.self = globalThis; global.fetch ||= require('node-fetch')`. For CI we added a small setup script referenced by vitest `setupFiles` to normalize globals.

Juan: There's also a TypeScript annoyance: tests importing types from default export hit TS2749. We fixed this by publishing an index.d.ts that re-exports both named and default types, and by adding explicit exports/exports.map in package.json: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" } }, "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts". That helps TS and bundlers consistently resolve shapes.

Alex: We should also stop relying on `export default new Client()` across builds. Instead ship `export class Client` + `export default Client` and ensure CJS build sets `module.exports = { default: Client, Client }` or similar so both worlds see the same API surface. That makes mocking and typings consistent.

Maya: Actionable plan: 1) I will add a short example vitest config and a test in sdk/examples that imports the SDK both ways and runs in CI; 2) Juan will add index.d.ts re-exports and adjust package.json exports/types; 3) Alex will adjust the build to export both named/default shapes in CJS; 4) Sam will add a CONTRIBUTING note about testing in monorepos (pnpm hoisting, deps.inline).

Juan: I'll also add a tiny GH Actions job that runs the examples test from the workspace root to catch hoisting issues early.

ci-bot: When you open the PR, CI will run the matrix including node18. Logs will indicate any remaining ESM transform failures. Good luck! :rocket:

Maya: Thanks team — I'll open the examples/docs PR in ~90 minutes and tag folks for reviews. :thumbsup:
